title: Book One · Chapter 115: The Sentence Under the Stall
story:
Ronan writes a sentence under his picture.

Mr Qiu lost his books and needs our money.

He looks at the words. They sound important. He draws a little box beside the words. People could write their names there to offer help.

Then he crosses out money and writes help instead. He has no permission to collect money. He knows that much.

He leaves the first half of the sentence unchanged. It still reads, “Mr Qiu lost his books.” Ronan is thinking of the six damp books. He is not thinking of the two dry crates.

He wants to take the picture to school. Miss Wu might put it on the wall. People can learn about the closed stall. Perhaps Mr Qiu will find a new place sooner.

Mum comes in while he is adding rain lines above the roof.

“Who read these words?” she asks.

“Me.”

“Has Mr Qiu agreed?”

“He liked the stall picture.”

“Those are different things.”

Ronan feels the familiar heat in his face. “I am trying to help.”

“I can see that. Show him first. Do not put it up yet.”

She leaves the paper with him. She does not hide it or carry it to Mr Qiu herself.

He waits until Mr Qiu comes to check his stock that evening. The rain is lighter, and Dad is still away. Ronan stands near the kitchen door with the drawing in both hands.

“Would this help?” he asks.

Mr Qiu takes time to read. His eyes move from the little stall to the sentence below it.

“No,” he says.

Ronan's hands tighten.

“I changed money.”

“I still have most of my books. Most are dry. What help do I need? You did not ask me first.”

“I can change lost.”

“That is not the only part. Do not write a story about my private money.”

“There is no money word now.”

Mr Qiu looks at him. “Your sentence asks everyone for help. Some people may think, ‘He needs money.’ You put a box for help below it.”

Ronan looks down. He imagined happy customers and Mr Qiu's smile. He did not think about Mr Qiu's feelings. Mr Qiu says no to this money story. Now Ronan knows that.

“It is only a draft,” he says.

“Good. Then keep it off the school wall.”

Mr Qiu hands it back carefully. He does not tear it. That almost makes Ronan feel worse. Now Ronan needs to choose a next step.

Mum is close enough to hear. “Do you want tea?” she asks Mr Qiu. He says not tonight. He needs to go and speak to someone about a possible counter space.

After he leaves, Ronan folds the drawing in half. The stall disappears inside the fold. The sentence is still there.

“Was he very angry?” he asks Mum.

“He said no to the story about money.”

“Will he let me help again?”

“You wrote about him. You did not ask first. You kept it at home. Now you need to put that right.”

Ronan wants her to tell him the exact words. “Which part is wrong?” she asks first.

He opens the folded paper again. Most books are dry, but his sentence says otherwise. He wrote first and did not ask Mr Qiu. Mr Qiu can say yes or no.

“Shall I throw it away?” he asks.

“Do you want to throw it away?”

“I do not want to look at that sentence.”

“You can cover it while you think. But remember your sentence. You need to speak to him about those words.”

Ronan finds a plain strip of paper. He lays it over the sentence. He can still see the stall picture above it. The white paper hides the sentence. The mistake is still there. But now he can look at the drawing alone. Mr Qiu may want to use it, or say no.

He writes those three things on a separate scrap. The drawing stays in his folder overnight. He showed it only to Mum and Mr Qiu. He still needs to ask Mr Qiu about the picture.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- draft＝草稿
- ask first＝先询问
- private＝私人的
- put that right＝把那件事改正

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：strip＝纸条；counter space＝柜台空间。

## 读句提示

**Which part is wrong?**

哪一部分／不对？直接问纸上哪处错，不叠what he knows is wrong。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan的句子错在事实与尊重两方面的哪里？
2. 为什么“我想帮忙”不能代替MrQiu本人的同意？
